resource.name: aws_cognito_user_pool
resource.description: Provides a Cognito User Pool resource.
resource.llm_summary: "Enables the creation and management of an Amazon Cognito User Pool, a scalable identity provider for user authentication and authorization in web and mobile applications. Common use cases include setting up secure user sign-up and sign-in flows, integrating social identity providers (e.g., Google, Facebook), and implementing multi-factor authentication (MFA). Supports configuration of user attributes, password policies, account recovery options, and advanced security features like adaptive authentication and risk-based access controls."

examples.title: Basic configuration
examples.llm_summary: "Demonstrates the basic configuration of an AWS Cognito User Pool using the `name` argument to define a pool with a custom name (`mypool`). This example is ideal for users looking to set up a minimal Cognito User Pool as a starting point for identity management in AWS."

examples.title: Enabling SMS and Software Token Multi-Factor Authentication
examples.llm_summary: This example demonstrates how to configure multi-factor authentication (MFA) for an AWS Cognito User Pool by enabling both SMS-based and software token MFA. It showcases key configurations such as the `mfa_configuration` argument, the `sms_configuration` block for integrating with Amazon SNS, and the `software_token_mfa_configuration` block to enable software token-based authentication.

examples.title: Using Account Recovery Setting
examples.llm_summary: This example demonstrates how to configure the `account_recovery_setting` block in the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource to define prioritized recovery mechanisms using `verified_email` and `verified_phone_number`. It illustrates how to set up account recovery options with specific priorities, enabling users to customize the recovery process for Cognito user pools.

arguments.name: alias_attributes
arguments.description: (Optional) Attributes supported as an alias for this user pool. Valid values: `phone_number`, `email`, or `preferred_username`. Conflicts with `username_attributes`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `alias_attributes` argument in the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource allows users to define alternative identifiers (aliases) for user authentication, such as `phone_number`, `email`, or `preferred_username`. Configuring this argument enables flexibility in how users log in to the Cognito user pool, enhancing the user experience by supporting multiple authentication methods. Note that it conflicts with `username_attributes`.

arguments.name: auto_verified_attributes
arguments.description: (Optional) Attributes to be auto-verified. Valid values: `email`, `phone_number`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `auto_verified_attributes` argument in the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource allows users to specify which user attributes, such as `email` or `phone_number`, should be automatically verified by Amazon Cognito during the user registration or sign-up process. Configuring this enhances user account validation workflows by reducing the need for manual verification, improving security and user experience.

arguments.name: deletion_protection
arguments.description: (Optional) When active, DeletionProtection prevents accidental deletion of your user pool. Before you can delete a user pool that you have protected against deletion, you must deactivate this feature. Valid values are `ACTIVE` and `INACTIVE`, Default value is `INACTIVE`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `deletion_protection` argument for the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource allows users to define whether accidental deletion of the user pool is prevented by enabling or disabling deletion protection. Setting this argument to `ACTIVE` ensures the user pool cannot be deleted without first deactivating the protection, supporting lifecycle management and safeguarding critical authentication infrastructure.

arguments.name: email_verification_message
arguments.description: (Optional) String representing the email verification message. Conflicts with `verification_message_template` configuration block `email_message` argument.
arguments.llm_summary: The `email_verification_message` argument in the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource allows users to define the custom email content sent to users for verifying their email addresses during account creation or recovery. By setting this argument, users can personalize the verification message to align with branding or communication requirements, but it cannot be used alongside the `verification_message_template.email_message` block, ensuring configuration consistency.

arguments.name: email_verification_subject
arguments.description: (Optional) String representing the email verification subject. Conflicts with `verification_message_template` configuration block `email_subject` argument.
arguments.llm_summary: The `email_verification_subject` argument allows users to define the subject line of the email sent to verify user accounts in the Cognito user pool, enabling customization of the verification process to align with branding or communication preferences. This argument directly impacts the user experience during account verification and cannot be used alongside the `verification_message_template.email_subject` configuration block.

arguments.name: id
arguments.llm_summary: The `id` argument in the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource represents the unique identifier of the Cognito User Pool. While optional, it allows users to reference or specify the User Pool's ID for integration with other resources or workflows, enabling seamless management and interaction with the pool in their cloud infrastructure.

arguments.name: mfa_configuration
arguments.description: (Optional) Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) configuration for the User Pool. Defaults of `OFF`. Valid values are `OFF` (MFA Tokens are not required), `ON` (MFA is required for all users to sign in; requires at least one of `sms_configuration` or `software_token_mfa_configuration` to be configured), or `OPTIONAL` (MFA Will be required only for individual users who have MFA Enabled; requires at least one of `sms_configuration` or `software_token_mfa_configuration` to be configured).
arguments.llm_summary: The `mfa_configuration` argument in the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource allows users to define the Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) behavior for the user pool, specifying whether MFA is disabled (`OFF`), mandatory for all users (`ON`), or optional for individual users (`OPTIONAL`). Configuring this argument impacts the security requirements for user sign-in, enabling enhanced authentication mechanisms when paired with `sms_configuration` or `software_token_mfa_configuration`.

arguments.name: name
arguments.description: (Required) Name of the user pool. The following arguments are optional:
arguments.llm_summary: The `name` argument for the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource specifies the unique identifier for the user pool, allowing users to define a meaningful and recognizable name for the pool. Setting this argument is essential for organizing and managing user authentication systems, as it serves as the primary reference for the user pool across AWS services and integrations.

arguments.name: sms_authentication_message
arguments.description: (Optional) String representing the SMS authentication message. The Message must contain the `{####}` placeholder, which will be replaced with the code.
arguments.llm_summary: The `sms_authentication_message` argument allows users to define the content of the SMS message sent to users for multi-factor authentication (MFA) in the `aws_cognito_user_pool`. This message must include the `{{####}}` placeholder, which is dynamically replaced with the authentication code, enabling secure and customizable communication for user verification workflows.

arguments.name: sms_verification_message
arguments.description: (Optional) String representing the SMS verification message. Conflicts with `verification_message_template` configuration block `sms_message` argument.
arguments.llm_summary: The `sms_verification_message` argument allows users to define the custom SMS message sent to users for account verification in the `aws_cognito_user_pool`. By configuring this, users can personalize the content of verification messages to align with branding or communication requirements, ensuring a tailored user experience. Note that it conflicts with the `verification_message_template.sms_message` argument.

arguments.name: tags
arguments.description: (Optional) Map of tags to assign to the User Pool. If configured with a provider `default_tags` configuration block present, tags with matching keys will overwrite those defined at the provider-level.
arguments.llm_summary: The `tags` argument for the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource allows users to assign metadata in the form of key-value pairs to the User Pool, enabling resource categorization, organization, and cost tracking. By setting this argument, users can define tags for purposes such as identifying environments (e.g., "dev" or "prod"), managing billing, or applying governance policies, with the ability to override provider-level default tags if configured.

arguments.name: tags_all
arguments.llm_summary: The `tags_all` argument in the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource allows users to define a comprehensive set of key-value tags that are automatically propagated to the user pool and any associated resources. This enables streamlined resource organization, cost allocation, and environment-specific tagging, supporting common goals like governance, tracking, and compliance across cloud infrastructure.

arguments.name: user_pool_tier
arguments.description: (Optional) The user pool feature plan, or tier. Valid values: `LITE`, `ESSENTIALS`, `PLUS`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `user_pool_tier` argument for the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource allows users to specify the feature plan or tier of the Cognito user pool, defining its capabilities and service level. Setting this argument impacts the functionality and cost of the user pool, enabling users to choose between tiers like `LITE`, `ESSENTIALS`, or `PLUS` to align with their application's requirements and budget.

arguments.name: username_attributes
arguments.description: (Optional) Whether email addresses or phone numbers can be specified as usernames when a user signs up. Conflicts with `alias_attributes`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `username_attributes` argument in the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource allows users to define whether email addresses or phone numbers can be used as usernames during user sign-up, enabling flexible authentication options tailored to user preferences. Setting this argument configures the user pool to accept these attributes as unique identifiers, enhancing the sign-up experience and supporting diverse login methods, but it cannot be used alongside `alias_attributes`.

blocks.name: account_recovery_setting
blocks.description: (Optional) Configuration block to define which verified available method a user can use to recover their forgotten password. Detailed below.

blocks.name: recovery_mechanism
blocks.description: (Optional) List of Account Recovery Options of the following structure:`name` - (Required) Recovery method for a user. Can be of the following: `verified_email`, `verified_phone_number`, and `admin_only`. `priority` - (Required) Positive integer specifying priority of a method with 1 being the highest priority.

arguments.name: name
arguments.description: (Required) Recovery method for a user. Can be of the following: `verified_email`, `verified_phone_number`, and `admin_only`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `name` argument in the `recovery_mechanism` block of the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource specifies the method used to recover user accounts, allowing you to define whether recovery is based on `verified_email`, `verified_phone_number`, or restricted to `admin_only`. By setting this argument, you control the recovery behavior for users, aligning it with your security and accessibility requirements for account recovery processes.

arguments.name: priority
arguments.description: (Required) Positive integer specifying priority of a method with 1 being the highest priority.
arguments.llm_summary: The `priority` argument for the `recovery_mechanism` in the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource allows users to define the order of preference for account recovery methods, with lower numerical values (e.g., 1) indicating higher priority. By configuring this required positive integer, users can control which recovery mechanism is attempted first, ensuring a tailored and efficient recovery process aligned with their application's user experience goals.

blocks.llm_summary: The `recovery_mechanism` block within the `account_recovery_setting` of the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource defines the prioritized methods for user account recovery, such as `verified_email`, `verified_phone_number`, or `admin_only`. By configuring this block, users can establish a structured hierarchy of recovery options to ensure secure and efficient account recovery workflows tailored to their application's needs.

The `account_recovery_setting` block in the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource configures methods for user password recovery, specifying which verified contact options (e.g., email or phone) can be used. This block enables fine-grained control over account recovery mechanisms, enhancing user experience and security by defining recovery workflows tailored to the application's needs.

blocks.name: admin_create_user_config
blocks.description: (Optional) Configuration block for creating a new user profile. Detailed below.

arguments.name: allow_admin_create_user_only
arguments.description: (Optional) Set to True if only the administrator is allowed to create user profiles. Set to False if users can sign themselves up via an app.
arguments.llm_summary: The `allow_admin_create_user_only` argument in the `admin_create_user_config` block of the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource controls whether user profiles can only be created by administrators or if users are allowed to self-register via an application. Setting this to `true` enforces administrative control over user creation, aligning with stricter access management policies, while setting it to `false` enables self-service user sign-up, supporting user-driven onboarding workflows.

blocks.name: invite_message_template
blocks.description: (Optional) Invite message template structure. Detailed below.

arguments.name: email_message
arguments.description: (Optional) Message template for email messages. Must contain `{username}` and `{####}` placeholders, for username and temporary password, respectively.
arguments.llm_summary: The `email_message` argument in the `invite_message_template` block of the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource allows users to define the custom content of email invitations sent to new Cognito users. By specifying this string, users can control the format and messaging of the email, ensuring it includes placeholders `{{username}}` and `{{####}}` for dynamically inserting the recipient's username and temporary password, respectively, to streamline user onboarding and authentication workflows.

arguments.name: email_subject
arguments.description: (Optional) Subject line for email messages.
arguments.llm_summary: The `email_subject` argument in the `invite_message_template` block of the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource allows users to define the subject line for invitation emails sent to new users. By configuring this optional string, users can customize the messaging to align with branding, improve user engagement, or provide context for the invitation, enhancing the overall onboarding experience.

arguments.name: sms_message
arguments.description: (Optional) Message template for SMS messages. Must contain `{username}` and `{####}` placeholders, for username and temporary password, respectively.
arguments.llm_summary: The `sms_message` argument allows users to define a custom SMS message template for user invitations in the `invite_message_template` of an `aws_cognito_user_pool`. This message must include the `{{username}}` and `{{####}}` placeholders to dynamically insert the recipient's username and temporary password, enabling personalized and compliant communication during the user onboarding process.

blocks.llm_summary: The `invite_message_template` block within the `admin_create_user_config` of the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource defines the structure and content of invitation messages sent to new users during account creation. It encapsulates settings for customizing email and SMS templates, enabling detailed control over the messaging format and content to align with branding or communication requirements, ensuring a seamless onboarding experience.

The `admin_create_user_config` block within the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource defines settings for managing the creation of user profiles by administrators, including options for temporary passwords, user invitation messages, and account activation workflows. Configuring this block enables fine-grained control over how new users are onboarded, ensuring a secure and customizable user creation process tailored to organizational requirements.

blocks.name: device_configuration
blocks.description: (Optional) Configuration block for the user pool's device tracking. Detailed below.

arguments.name: challenge_required_on_new_device
arguments.description: (Optional) Whether a challenge is required on a new device. Only applicable to a new device.
arguments.llm_summary: Controls whether a security challenge is enforced for users signing in from a new device within the Cognito user pool's device configuration. Enabling this enhances account security by requiring additional verification for unrecognized devices, aligning with common goals of securing user authentication workflows.

arguments.name: device_only_remembered_on_user_prompt
arguments.description: (Optional) Whether a device is only remembered on user prompt. `false` equates to "Always" remember, `true` is "User Opt In," and not using a `device_configuration` block is "No."
arguments.llm_summary: Controls whether user devices in the Cognito user pool are remembered automatically or only upon explicit user consent. Setting this to `true` enables a "User Opt In" behavior, requiring users to confirm device remembrance, while `false` ensures devices are always remembered, aligning with user authentication and device management preferences.

blocks.llm_summary: The `device_configuration` block in the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource enables device tracking and management within the user pool, allowing for enhanced security and user experience. It encapsulates settings related to remembering and tracking devices, helping users configure features like device remembering preferences and multi-factor authentication (MFA) requirements for trusted devices.

blocks.name: email_configuration
blocks.description: (Optional) Configuration block for configuring email. Detailed below.

arguments.name: configuration_set
arguments.description: (Optional) Email configuration set name from SES.
arguments.llm_summary: The `configuration_set` argument in the `email_configuration` block of the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource allows users to specify the name of an Amazon SES configuration set to manage email delivery settings for user pool communications. By defining this, users can control advanced email behaviors such as tracking, feedback handling, or applying custom rules, aligning with goals like optimizing email delivery and monitoring performance.

arguments.name: email_sending_account
arguments.description: (Optional) Email delivery method to use. `COGNITO_DEFAULT` for the default email functionality built into Cognito or `DEVELOPER` to use your Amazon SES configuration. Required to be `DEVELOPER` if `from_email_address` is set.
arguments.llm_summary: The `email_sending_account` argument in the `email_configuration` block of the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource specifies the email delivery method for user pool communications. It allows users to choose between Cognito's default email functionality (`COGNITO_DEFAULT`) or a custom Amazon SES configuration (`DEVELOPER`), enabling greater control over email branding and delivery. Setting this to `DEVELOPER` is required when using a custom `from_email_address`, aligning with common goals of customizing email sender details and improving deliverability.

arguments.name: from_email_address
arguments.description: (Optional) Sender’s email address or sender’s display name with their email address (e.g., `john@example.com`, `John Smith <john@example.com>` or `\"John Smith Ph.D.\" <john@example.com>`). Escaped double quotes are required around display names that contain certain characters as specified in RFC 5322.
arguments.llm_summary: Defines the sender's email address or display name with an email address for outgoing messages in the user pool's email configuration. This argument allows users to customize the "From" field in emails sent by AWS Cognito, enabling branding or personalization for communication with end users.

arguments.name: reply_to_email_address
arguments.description: (Optional) REPLY-TO email address.
arguments.llm_summary: The `reply_to_email_address` argument in the `email_configuration` block of the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource allows users to specify the email address that will appear as the "Reply-To" address in outgoing emails sent by the user pool. Configuring this ensures that responses to system-generated emails, such as account verification or password recovery, are directed to a designated email address, enhancing communication management and user support workflows.

arguments.name: source_arn
arguments.description: (Optional) ARN of the SES verified email identity to use. Required if `email_sending_account` is set to `DEVELOPER`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `source_arn` argument in the `email_configuration` block of the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource specifies the ARN of an SES-verified email identity to be used as the sender for outgoing emails. This is required when the `email_sending_account` is set to `DEVELOPER`, enabling users to configure a custom email sender for user pool communications, such as account verification or password recovery emails.

blocks.llm_summary: The `email_configuration` block in the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource defines settings for managing email delivery, including sender details and delivery mechanisms, such as using Amazon SES or the default Cognito email service. Configuring this block allows users to customize email communication for user pool operations, such as account verification and password recovery, ensuring alignment with branding and compliance requirements.

blocks.name: email_mfa_configuration
blocks.description: (Optional) Configuration block for configuring email Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA); requires at least 2 `account_recovery_setting` entries; requires an `email_configuration` configuration block. Detailed below.

arguments.name: message
arguments.description: (Optional) The template for the email messages that your user pool sends to users with codes for MFA and sign-in with email OTPs. The message must contain the {####} placeholder. In the message, Amazon Cognito replaces this placeholder with the code. If you don't provide this parameter, Amazon Cognito sends messages in the default format.
arguments.llm_summary: The `message` argument in the `email_mfa_configuration` of the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource allows users to define a custom email template for MFA and email OTP sign-in codes, specifying the content and format of the messages sent to users. By setting this argument, users can personalize the email communication experience while ensuring the required `{{####}}` placeholder is included for code substitution, otherwise default messaging is used.

arguments.name: subject
arguments.description: (Optional) The subject of the email messages that your user pool sends to users with codes for MFA and email OTP sign-in.
arguments.llm_summary: The `subject` argument in the `email_mfa_configuration` of the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource allows users to define the subject line for email messages sent to users during MFA or email OTP sign-in processes. By configuring this, users can customize the email content to align with branding or communication standards, enhancing the user experience and ensuring clarity in authentication workflows.

blocks.llm_summary: The `email_mfa_configuration` block within the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource enables the setup of email-based Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) for enhanced user account security. It encapsulates related settings that require integration with `email_configuration` and at least two `account_recovery_setting` entries, allowing users to enforce MFA via email and improve account recovery mechanisms for secure authentication workflows.

blocks.name: lambda_config
blocks.description: (Optional) Configuration block for the AWS Lambda triggers associated with the user pool. Detailed below.

arguments.name: create_auth_challenge
arguments.description: (Optional) ARN of the lambda creating an authentication challenge.
arguments.llm_summary: The `create_auth_challenge` argument in the `lambda_config` block of the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource specifies the ARN of a Lambda function responsible for generating custom authentication challenges during the user sign-in process. By configuring this argument, users can define tailored challenge flows to enhance security or implement advanced authentication mechanisms, aligning with specific application requirements.

arguments.name: custom_message
arguments.description: (Optional) Custom Message AWS Lambda trigger.
arguments.llm_summary: The `custom_message` argument in the `lambda_config` block of the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource allows users to specify an AWS Lambda function that customizes the content and behavior of messages sent by the user pool, such as email or SMS notifications. By configuring this, users can tailor communication workflows to meet specific branding, localization, or user engagement requirements.

arguments.name: define_auth_challenge
arguments.description: (Optional) Defines the authentication challenge.
arguments.llm_summary: The `define_auth_challenge` argument in the `lambda_config` block of the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource specifies the name of an AWS Lambda function that customizes the authentication challenge flow for users. By setting this argument, users can define tailored challenge logic, such as multi-factor authentication or custom validation steps, to enhance security and control over the user authentication process.

arguments.name: kms_key_id
arguments.description: (Optional) The Amazon Resource Name of Key Management Service Customer master keys. Amazon Cognito uses the key to encrypt codes and temporary passwords sent to CustomEmailSender and CustomSMSSender.
arguments.llm_summary: The `kms_key_id` argument in the `lambda_config` block of the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource allows users to specify the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of a KMS Customer Master Key (CMK) for encrypting sensitive data, such as codes and temporary passwords, sent by custom Lambda functions for email and SMS delivery. Configuring this argument enhances security by enabling encryption of communication between Cognito and custom sender functions, aligning with compliance and data protection goals.

arguments.name: post_authentication
arguments.description: (Optional) Post-authentication AWS Lambda trigger.
arguments.llm_summary: The `post_authentication` argument in the `lambda_config` block of the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource allows users to specify an AWS Lambda function that triggers after a user successfully authenticates. This enables custom post-authentication workflows, such as updating user attributes, logging events, or integrating with external systems, to enhance user management and security processes.

arguments.name: post_confirmation
arguments.description: (Optional) Post-confirmation AWS Lambda trigger.
arguments.llm_summary: The `post_confirmation` argument in the `lambda_config` block of the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource allows users to specify an AWS Lambda function that is triggered after a user successfully confirms their account. This enables custom post-confirmation workflows, such as sending welcome emails, updating user attributes, or integrating with external systems, to enhance user onboarding and automate post-registration processes.

arguments.name: pre_authentication
arguments.description: (Optional) Pre-authentication AWS Lambda trigger.
arguments.llm_summary: The `pre_authentication` argument in the `lambda_config` block of the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource allows users to specify an AWS Lambda function that triggers before user authentication occurs. This enables custom pre-authentication logic, such as validating user attributes or implementing additional security checks, to tailor the authentication process to specific application requirements.

arguments.name: pre_sign_up
arguments.description: (Optional) Pre-registration AWS Lambda trigger.
arguments.llm_summary: The `pre_sign_up` argument in the `lambda_config` block of the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource allows users to specify an AWS Lambda function that triggers before a user registers in the Cognito user pool. This enables custom pre-registration logic, such as validating user attributes, implementing custom approval workflows, or blocking sign-ups based on specific criteria, enhancing control over the user onboarding process.

arguments.name: pre_token_generation
arguments.description: (Optional) Allow to customize identity token claims before token generation. Set this parameter for legacy purposes; for new instances of pre token generation triggers, set the lambda_arn of `pre_token_generation_config`.
arguments.llm_summary: "Configures a legacy Lambda trigger to customize identity token claims before token generation in the Cognito user pool. This argument allows users to specify the ARN of a pre-token generation Lambda function, enabling tailored token content for authentication workflows, but is recommended only for backward compatibility as newer configurations use `pre_token_generation_config`."

arguments.name: user_migration
arguments.description: (Optional) User migration Lambda config type.
arguments.llm_summary: The `user_migration` argument in the `lambda_config` block of the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource allows users to specify the ARN of a Lambda function that handles user migration during authentication. This enables seamless migration of users from an external identity store or legacy system into the Cognito user pool, ensuring continuity and a smooth transition for authentication workflows.

arguments.name: verify_auth_challenge_response
arguments.description: (Optional) Verifies the authentication challenge response.
arguments.llm_summary: The `verify_auth_challenge_response` argument in the `lambda_config` block of the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource specifies the ARN of a Lambda function that validates the user's response to an authentication challenge during custom authentication workflows. Configuring this argument enables custom logic for verifying challenge responses, allowing fine-grained control over authentication behavior and enhancing security or user-specific requirements.

blocks.name: custom_email_sender
blocks.description: (Optional) A custom email sender AWS Lambda trigger. See custom_email_sender Below.

arguments.name: lambda_arn
arguments.description: (Required) The Lambda Amazon Resource Name of the Lambda function that Amazon Cognito triggers to send email notifications to users.
arguments.llm_summary: The `lambda_arn` argument for the `custom_email_sender` in the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Lambda function that handles custom email notifications for user interactions, such as account creation or password resets. By setting this required argument, users can define a custom email-sending workflow, enabling tailored communication and branding for their Cognito user pool.

arguments.name: lambda_version
arguments.description: (Required) The Lambda version represents the signature of the "request" attribute in the "event" information Amazon Cognito passes to your custom email Lambda function. The only supported value is `V1_0`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `lambda_version` argument specifies the version of the Lambda function signature used by the `custom_email_sender` in an Amazon Cognito user pool, ensuring compatibility with the event structure (`V1_0`) passed by Cognito. Setting this argument enables the user to define the expected request format for their custom email Lambda function, facilitating seamless integration and proper handling of email-sending events.

blocks.llm_summary: "Defines a custom email sender trigger within the `lambda_config` of an AWS Cognito User Pool, enabling integration with an AWS Lambda function to handle email delivery logic. This block allows users to customize email workflows, such as branding or dynamic content, by specifying Lambda-based processing for outgoing emails."

blocks.name: custom_sms_sender
blocks.description: (Optional) A custom SMS sender AWS Lambda trigger. See custom_sms_sender Below.

arguments.name: lambda_arn
arguments.description: (Required) The Lambda Amazon Resource Name of the Lambda function that Amazon Cognito triggers to send SMS notifications to users.
arguments.llm_summary: The `lambda_arn` argument specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Lambda function that Amazon Cognito invokes to send SMS notifications, enabling users to define a custom SMS sender for their Cognito user pool. By configuring this required parameter, users can implement tailored messaging logic, such as branding or dynamic content, to enhance user communication and meet specific business requirements.

arguments.name: lambda_version
arguments.description: (Required) The Lambda version represents the signature of the "request" attribute in the "event" information Amazon Cognito passes to your custom SMS Lambda function. The only supported value is `V1_0`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `lambda_version` argument specifies the version of the request signature format (`V1_0`) used by Amazon Cognito when invoking the custom SMS sender Lambda function, ensuring compatibility with the event structure passed to the function. This required configuration enables users to define the behavior and integration of their custom SMS sender, aligning it with Cognito's expected event schema for seamless execution.

blocks.llm_summary: The `custom_sms_sender` block within the `lambda_config` of the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource enables the configuration of a custom AWS Lambda function to handle SMS delivery for user pool operations. It encapsulates settings related to integrating a custom SMS sender, allowing users to override the default SMS delivery mechanism and achieve greater control over messaging workflows, such as customizing sender logic or integrating third-party services.

blocks.name: pre_token_generation_config
blocks.description: (Optional) Allow to customize access tokens. See pre_token_configuration_type

arguments.name: lambda_arn
arguments.llm_summary: The `lambda_arn` argument in the `pre_token_generation_config` of the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS Lambda function to be invoked during the pre-token generation event. This allows users to customize token claims or implement advanced validation logic before tokens are issued, enabling tailored authentication workflows and dynamic user attribute modifications.

arguments.name: lambda_version
arguments.llm_summary: The `lambda_version` argument in the `pre_token_generation_config` of the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource specifies the version of the AWS Lambda function used for customizing token generation during user authentication. Setting this argument ensures the correct Lambda function version is invoked, enabling precise control over pre-token generation logic, such as modifying claims or adding custom attributes to tokens.

blocks.llm_summary: The `pre_token_generation_config` block within the `lambda_config` of the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource enables customization of access tokens by integrating a pre-token generation Lambda trigger. It encapsulates settings related to invoking a Lambda function to modify claims or attributes in tokens before they are issued, allowing users to implement advanced token customization logic for enhanced security, compliance, or application-specific requirements.

The `lambda_config` block in the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource enables the integration of AWS Lambda triggers to customize and extend user pool workflows, such as user authentication, registration, and account recovery. It encapsulates settings for specifying Lambda function ARNs for various trigger types, allowing users to implement advanced logic and automation tailored to their application's identity management needs.

blocks.name: password_policy
blocks.description: (Optional) Configuration block for information about the user pool password policy. Detailed below.

arguments.name: minimum_length
arguments.description: (Optional) Minimum length of the password policy that you have set.
arguments.llm_summary: The `minimum_length` argument in the `password_policy` block of the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource allows users to define the minimum number of characters required for passwords in the user pool, enhancing security by enforcing stronger password requirements. Configuring this parameter helps align password policies with organizational or compliance standards, ensuring user credentials meet a baseline level of complexity.

arguments.name: password_history_size
arguments.description: (Optional) Number of previous passwords that you want Amazon Cognito to restrict each user from reusing. Users can't set a password that matches any of number of previous passwords specified by this argument. A value of 0 means that password history is not enforced. Valid values are between 0 and 24. Note: This argument requires advanced security features to be active in the user pool.
arguments.llm_summary: The `password_history_size` argument in the `password_policy` block of the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource allows users to define the number of previous passwords Amazon Cognito will prevent users from reusing, enhancing account security by enforcing password uniqueness. Setting this argument configures the password reuse restriction, with valid values ranging from 0 (no restriction) to 24, and requires advanced security features to be enabled in the user pool.

arguments.name: require_lowercase
arguments.description: (Optional) Whether you have required users to use at least one lowercase letter in their password.
arguments.llm_summary: The `require_lowercase` argument in the `password_policy` block of the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource allows users to enforce password complexity by requiring at least one lowercase letter in user passwords. Configuring this option enhances security by ensuring stronger password policies, aligning with compliance standards and reducing the risk of unauthorized access.

arguments.name: require_numbers
arguments.description: (Optional) Whether you have required users to use at least one number in their password.
arguments.llm_summary: The `require_numbers` argument in the `password_policy` block of the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource allows users to enforce password complexity by requiring at least one numeric character in user passwords. This configuration enhances security by ensuring stronger password policies, aligning with common compliance and user authentication goals.

arguments.name: require_symbols
arguments.description: (Optional) Whether you have required users to use at least one symbol in their password.
arguments.llm_summary: The `require_symbols` argument in the `password_policy` block of the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource allows users to enforce password complexity by requiring at least one symbol in user passwords. This enhances security by ensuring stronger password policies, aligning with compliance or organizational standards for user authentication.

arguments.name: require_uppercase
arguments.description: (Optional) Whether you have required users to use at least one uppercase letter in their password.
arguments.llm_summary: Controls whether the password policy for the Cognito user pool enforces the inclusion of at least one uppercase letter in user passwords. Setting this argument to `true` enhances password complexity and security, aligning with common compliance and user authentication best practices.

arguments.name: temporary_password_validity_days
arguments.description: (Optional) In the password policy you have set, refers to the number of days a temporary password is valid. If the user does not sign-in during this time, their password will need to be reset by an administrator. minimum_length - (Optional) Minimum length of the password policy that you have set. password_history_size - (Optional) Number of previous passwords that you want Amazon Cognito to restrict each user from reusing. Users can't set a password that matches any of number of previous passwords specified by this argument. A value of 0 means that password history is not enforced. Valid values are between 0 and 24. Note: This argument requires advanced security features to be active in the user pool. require_lowercase - (Optional) Whether you have required users to use at least one lowercase letter in their password. require_numbers - (Optional) Whether you have required users to use at least one number in their password. require_symbols - (Optional) Whether you have required users to use at least one symbol in their password. require_uppercase - (Optional) Whether you have required users to use at least one uppercase letter in their password. temporary_password_validity_days - (Optional) In the password policy you have set, refers to the number of days a temporary password is valid. If the user does not sign-in during this time, their password will need to be reset by an administrator.
arguments.llm_summary: The `temporary_password_validity_days` argument in the `password_policy` of the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource allows users to define the number of days a temporary password remains valid before requiring administrative reset if the user does not sign in. This configuration helps enforce security policies by controlling the lifespan of temporary credentials, ensuring timely user account activation and reducing exposure to unused passwords.

blocks.llm_summary: The `password_policy` configuration block within the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource defines rules and constraints for user passwords, enabling enhanced security and compliance for the user pool. It encapsulates settings such as password length, complexity requirements, and expiration policies, allowing users to enforce robust password standards tailored to their application's security needs.

blocks.name: schema
blocks.description: (Optional) Configuration block for the schema attributes of a user pool. Detailed below. Schema attributes from the standard attribute set only need to be specified if they are different from the default configuration. Attributes can be added, but not modified or removed. Maximum of 50 attributes.

arguments.name: attribute_data_type
arguments.description: (Required) Attribute data type. Must be one of `Boolean`, `Number`, `String`, `DateTime`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `attribute_data_type` argument in the `schema` block of the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource specifies the data type (`Boolean`, `Number`, `String`, or `DateTime`) for a custom user attribute in the Cognito user pool. By defining this, users control the format and validation rules for the attribute, ensuring proper data handling and enabling tailored user profile configurations to meet application-specific requirements.

arguments.name: developer_only_attribute
arguments.description: (Optional) Whether the attribute type is developer only.
arguments.llm_summary: The `developer_only_attribute` argument in the `schema` block of the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource allows users to specify whether a custom attribute is restricted for use exclusively by developers, preventing it from being accessible or modifiable by end users. Setting this to `true` enables the creation of attributes intended for backend or administrative purposes, supporting scenarios like internal tracking or system-level configurations.

arguments.name: mutable
arguments.description: (Optional) Whether the attribute can be changed once it has been created.
arguments.llm_summary: The `mutable` argument in the `schema` block of the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource allows users to specify whether a user attribute can be modified after its initial creation. Setting this to `true` enables flexibility for updates to the attribute, while `false` enforces immutability, which is useful for attributes requiring strict consistency, such as unique identifiers or sensitive data.

arguments.name: name
arguments.description: (Required) Name of the attribute.
arguments.llm_summary: The `name` argument in the `schema` block of the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource specifies the name of a custom attribute within the user pool's schema. By defining this argument, users can create and identify custom attributes that extend the default user profile, enabling tailored user data storage and supporting specific application requirements.

arguments.name: required
arguments.description: (Optional) Whether a user pool attribute is required. If the attribute is required and the user does not provide a value, registration or sign-in will fail.
arguments.llm_summary: The `required` argument in the `schema` block of the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource allows users to specify whether a user pool attribute must be provided during registration or sign-in. Setting this to `true` enforces stricter validation by requiring the attribute, ensuring compliance with application-specific user data requirements and preventing account creation or access without the specified attribute.

blocks.name: number_attribute_constraints
blocks.description: (Required when `attribute_data_type` is `Number`) Configuration block for the constraints for an attribute of the number type. Detailed below.

arguments.name: max_value
arguments.description: (Optional) Maximum value of an attribute that is of the number data type.
arguments.llm_summary: The `max_value` argument within the `number_attribute_constraints` block of the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource allows users to define the upper limit for attributes of the number data type in a Cognito user pool. By setting this value, users can enforce validation rules to restrict the maximum permissible numeric input for custom attributes, ensuring data integrity and compliance with application-specific requirements.

arguments.name: min_value
arguments.description: (Optional) Minimum value of an attribute that is of the number data type.
arguments.llm_summary: The `min_value` argument in the `number_attribute_constraints` block of the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource allows users to define the minimum acceptable value for a custom attribute of the number data type. This ensures that user-provided numeric inputs meet a specified lower boundary, enabling validation and enforcement of attribute constraints within the Cognito user pool.

blocks.llm_summary: The `number_attribute_constraints` block in the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource schema defines validation rules for attributes of the `Number` data type, ensuring they meet specific numerical constraints such as minimum and maximum values. Configuring this block allows users to enforce precise boundaries for numeric attributes, enhancing data integrity and compliance within the user pool.

blocks.name: string_attribute_constraints
blocks.description: (Required when `attribute_data_type` is `String`) Constraints for an attribute of the string type. Detailed below.

arguments.name: max_length
arguments.description: (Optional) Maximum length of an attribute value of the string type.
arguments.llm_summary: "Defines the maximum allowable length for string-type attribute values in the Cognito user pool, enabling control over data validation and ensuring compliance with application-specific constraints or user input requirements."

arguments.name: min_length
arguments.description: (Optional) Minimum length of an attribute value of the string type.
arguments.llm_summary: The `min_length` argument in the `string_attribute_constraints` block of the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource allows users to define the minimum number of characters required for string-type attributes in the user pool. By setting this value, users can enforce stricter validation rules for attribute inputs, ensuring compliance with specific data requirements or security policies.

blocks.llm_summary: "Defines validation rules for string-type attributes in the user pool schema, enabling constraints such as minimum and maximum length to ensure data integrity and compliance with application requirements."

The `schema` configuration block in the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource defines the attributes of user profiles within the pool, enabling customization of standard and custom attributes to meet specific application requirements. It allows users to specify up to 50 attributes, providing granular control over user data structure and validation, while ensuring compatibility with default configurations for standard attributes.

blocks.name: sign_in_policy
blocks.description: (Optional) Configuration block for information about the user pool sign in policy. Detailed below.

arguments.name: allowed_first_auth_factors
arguments.description: (Optional) The sign in methods your user pool supports as the first factor. This is a list of strings, allowed values are `PASSWORD`, `EMAIL_OTP`, `SMS_OTP`, and `WEB_AUTHN`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `allowed_first_auth_factors` argument in the `sign_in_policy` of the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource allows users to define the authentication methods supported as the initial factor during user sign-in. By specifying values such as `PASSWORD`, `EMAIL_OTP`, `SMS_OTP`, or `WEB_AUTHN`, this argument configures the user pool's sign-in behavior to align with desired security requirements and user experience goals, enabling flexible multi-factor authentication strategies.

blocks.llm_summary: The `sign_in_policy` configuration block within the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource defines rules and settings for user authentication and sign-in behavior, such as allowed sign-in methods and requirements. Configuring this block enables fine-grained control over how users authenticate, ensuring compliance with security policies and enhancing the user experience for accessing the Cognito user pool.

blocks.name: sms_configuration
blocks.description: (Optional) Configuration block for Short Message Service (SMS) settings. Detailed below. These settings apply to SMS user verification and SMS Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA). Due to Cognito API restrictions, the SMS configuration cannot be removed without recreating the Cognito User Pool. For user data safety, this resource will ignore the removal of this configuration by disabling drift detection. To force resource recreation after this configuration has been applied, see the `taint` command.

arguments.name: external_id
arguments.description: (Required) External ID used in IAM role trust relationships. For more information about using external IDs, see How to Use an External ID When Granting Access to Your AWS Resources to a Third Party.
arguments.llm_summary: The `external_id` argument in the `sms_configuration` block of the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource specifies a unique identifier used in IAM role trust relationships to securely delegate permissions for sending SMS messages via AWS. By defining this value, users ensure secure access control for third-party services or applications interacting with the user pool's SMS functionality, preventing unauthorized access and enhancing security.

arguments.name: sns_caller_arn
arguments.description: (Required) ARN of the Amazon SNS caller. This is usually the IAM role that you've given Cognito permission to assume.
arguments.llm_summary: The `sns_caller_arn` argument specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM role that Cognito is authorized to assume for sending SMS messages via Amazon SNS. By configuring this required parameter, users enable SMS functionality for their Cognito user pool, such as multi-factor authentication (MFA) or phone number verification, ensuring secure and reliable communication through the designated IAM role.

arguments.name: sns_region
arguments.description: (Optional) The AWS Region to use with Amazon SNS integration. You can choose the same Region as your user pool, or a supported Legacy Amazon SNS alternate Region. Amazon Cognito resources in the Asia Pacific (Seoul) AWS Region must use your Amazon SNS configuration in the Asia Pacific (Tokyo) Region. For more information, see SMS message settings for Amazon Cognito user pools.
arguments.llm_summary: The `sns_region` argument in the `sms_configuration` block of the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource allows users to specify the AWS Region for Amazon SNS integration, which is used to send SMS messages for user pool operations. Configuring this argument ensures compatibility with regional requirements and enables SMS functionality by aligning the SNS setup with either the user pool's Region or a supported alternate Region, such as for legacy or cross-Region use cases.

blocks.llm_summary: The `sms_configuration` block in the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource defines settings for SMS-based user verification and Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA), enabling secure communication with users via text messages. It encapsulates parameters for SMS delivery, such as sender details and service integration, ensuring reliable user authentication workflows. Configuring this block is essential for implementing SMS-based security features, but changes require recreating the user pool due to API restrictions.

blocks.name: software_token_mfa_configuration
blocks.description: (Optional) Configuration block for software token Mult-Factor Authentication (MFA) settings. Detailed below.

arguments.name: enabled
arguments.description: (Required) Boolean whether to enable software token Multi-Factor (MFA) tokens, such as Time-based One-Time Password (TOTP). To disable software token MFA When `sms_configuration` is not present, the `mfa_configuration` argument must be set to `OFF` and the `software_token_mfa_configuration` configuration block must be fully removed.
arguments.llm_summary: The `enabled` argument in the `software_token_mfa_configuration` block of the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource specifies whether software token-based Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA), such as Time-based One-Time Password (TOTP), is activated for the user pool. Setting this argument to `true` enables enhanced security by requiring users to authenticate using software token MFA, while disabling it requires alternative MFA configurations or turning MFA off entirely.

blocks.llm_summary: "Configures software token-based Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) settings within an AWS Cognito User Pool, enabling enhanced security for user authentication. This block encapsulates related settings to define and manage MFA behavior, allowing users to enforce or customize token-based MFA for improved account protection and compliance."

blocks.name: user_attribute_update_settings
blocks.description: (Optional) Configuration block for user attribute update settings. Detailed below.

arguments.name: attributes_require_verification_before_update
arguments.description: (Required) A list of attributes requiring verification before update. If set, the provided value(s) must also be set in `auto_verified_attributes`. Valid values: `email`, `phone_number`.
arguments.llm_summary: Defines the user attributes in the Cognito user pool that require verification (e.g., `email`, `phone_number`) before they can be updated, ensuring stricter security and compliance for sensitive data changes. This argument enables the enforcement of verification workflows for specified attributes, aligning with user goals of maintaining data integrity and secure account management.

blocks.llm_summary: The `user_attribute_update_settings` block in the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource configures rules and permissions for updating user attributes within the Cognito user pool. It enables fine-grained control over how and when user attributes can be modified, ensuring compliance with security and operational requirements for user data management.

blocks.name: user_pool_add_ons
blocks.description: (Optional) Configuration block for user pool add-ons to enable user pool advanced security mode features. Detailed below.

arguments.name: advanced_security_mode
arguments.description: (Required) Mode for advanced security, must be one of `OFF`, `AUDIT` or `ENFORCED`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `advanced_security_mode` argument in the `user_pool_add_ons` block of the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource allows users to define the level of advanced security features applied to the user pool, controlling how threats like compromised credentials are detected and mitigated. By setting this required argument to `OFF`, `AUDIT`, or `ENFORCED`, users can specify whether security features are disabled, monitored for suspicious activity, or actively enforced to block risky actions, aligning the user pool's behavior with compliance and security goals.

blocks.llm_summary: The `user_pool_add_ons` configuration block in the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource enables advanced security features for the user pool, such as adaptive authentication and risk-based analysis. It encapsulates settings related to enhancing security measures, helping users protect against unauthorized access and improve account safety through intelligent threat detection mechanisms.

blocks.name: username_configuration
blocks.description: (Optional) Configuration block for username configuration. Detailed below.

arguments.name: case_sensitive
arguments.description: (Optional) Whether username case sensitivity will be applied for all users in the user pool through Cognito APIs.
arguments.llm_summary: The `case_sensitive` argument in the `username_configuration` block of the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource allows users to specify whether usernames in the user pool are treated as case-sensitive when interacting with Cognito APIs. Enabling this setting ensures that usernames like "User123" and "user123" are considered distinct, providing stricter control over user identity management and authentication behavior.

blocks.llm_summary: The `username_configuration` block within the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource defines settings related to how usernames are handled in the user pool, specifically enabling or disabling case sensitivity for usernames. Configuring this block allows users to control username behavior, ensuring consistency and alignment with application requirements for user authentication and identity management.

blocks.name: verification_message_template
blocks.description: (Optional) Configuration block for verification message templates. Detailed below.

arguments.name: default_email_option
arguments.description: (Optional) Default email option. Must be either `CONFIRM_WITH_CODE` or `CONFIRM_WITH_LINK`. Defaults to `CONFIRM_WITH_CODE`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `default_email_option` argument in the `verification_message_template` block of the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource allows users to specify the default method for email-based user verification, either as a confirmation code (`CONFIRM_WITH_CODE`) or a clickable link (`CONFIRM_WITH_LINK`). This configuration impacts the user experience during account verification, enabling customization of the verification flow to align with application requirements or user preferences.

arguments.name: email_message
arguments.description: (Optional) Email message template. Must contain the `{####}` placeholder. Conflicts with `email_verification_message` argument.
arguments.llm_summary: The `email_message` argument in the `verification_message_template` block of the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource allows users to define a custom email template for verification messages sent to users. This template must include the `{{####}}` placeholder, which is replaced with the verification code, enabling personalized and branded communication during the user account verification process.

arguments.name: email_message_by_link
arguments.description: (Optional) Email message template for sending a confirmation link to the user, it must contain the `{##Click Here##}` placeholder.
arguments.llm_summary: Defines the email message template used to send a confirmation link to users during account verification, allowing customization of the content and ensuring it includes the required `{{##Click Here##}}` placeholder for the link. Configuring this argument enables tailored communication for user onboarding and verification workflows in the Cognito user pool.

arguments.name: email_subject
arguments.description: (Optional) Subject line for the email message template. Conflicts with `email_verification_subject` argument.
arguments.llm_summary: The `email_subject` argument in the `verification_message_template` block of the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource allows users to define the subject line for the email sent to verify user accounts. By configuring this optional string, users can customize the messaging to align with branding or communication goals, enhancing the user experience during account verification.

arguments.name: email_subject_by_link
arguments.description: (Optional) Subject line for the email message template for sending a confirmation link to the user.
arguments.llm_summary: Defines the subject line for the email sent to users containing a confirmation link, allowing customization of the verification message template to align with branding or communication goals. Configuring this argument ensures the email subject is tailored to enhance user experience and clarity during account verification.

arguments.name: sms_message
arguments.description: (Optional) SMS message template. Must contain the `{####}` placeholder. Conflicts with `sms_verification_message` argument.
arguments.llm_summary: The `sms_message` argument in the `verification_message_template` block of the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource allows users to define the SMS template sent to users for verification purposes. This message must include the `{{####}}` placeholder for the verification code, enabling customization of the content and format of SMS-based user authentication flows.

blocks.llm_summary: The `verification_message_template` block in the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource configures the content and delivery settings for user account verification messages, including email and SMS templates. This block enables detailed customization of verification messages, allowing users to tailor the user experience for account confirmation workflows and improve communication consistency within their Cognito user pool.

blocks.name: web_authn_configuration
blocks.description: (Optional) Configuration block for web authn configuration. Detailed below.

arguments.name: relying_party_id
arguments.description: (Optional) The authentication domain that passkeys providers use as a relying party.
arguments.llm_summary: The `relying_party_id` argument in the `web_authn_configuration` block of the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource specifies the authentication domain used by passkey providers as the relying party identifier. Configuring this value enables WebAuthn functionality by defining the domain that passkey-based authentication mechanisms will trust, aligning with user authentication goals for secure, domain-specific access.

arguments.name: user_verification
arguments.description: (Optional) If your user pool should require a passkey. Must be one of `required` or `preferred`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `user_verification` argument in the `web_authn_configuration` block of the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource allows users to specify the level of passkey-based authentication required for verifying end-user identities during WebAuthn interactions. By setting this to either `required` or `preferred`, users can control whether passkey verification is mandatory or optional, impacting the security and user experience of authentication workflows.

blocks.llm_summary: The `web_authn_configuration` block within the `aws_cognito_user_pool` resource enables the setup and management of WebAuthn authentication settings, facilitating secure, passwordless login experiences using biometric or hardware-based authenticators. This block encapsulates related settings for configuring WebAuthn parameters, such as credential types and user verification methods, allowing users to enhance authentication security and compliance with modern identity standards.

attributes.name: creation_date
attributes.description: Date the user pool was created.

attributes.name: custom_domain
attributes.description: A custom domain name that you provide to Amazon Cognito. This parameter applies only if you use a custom domain to host the sign-up and sign-in pages for your application. For example: `auth.example.com`.

attributes.name: domain
attributes.description: Holds the domain prefix if the user pool has a domain associated with it.

attributes.name: endpoint
attributes.description: Endpoint name of the user pool. Example format: `cognito-idp.REGION.amazonaws.com/xxxx_yyyyy`

attributes.name: estimated_number_of_users
attributes.description: A number estimating the size of the user pool.

attributes.name: last_modified_date
attributes.description: Date the user pool was last modified.
